office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, and confirms the governor's appointments, for a four-year term.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent June Robinson, chair of the Senate budget committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Brad Bender; Robinson took about two thirds of the primary vote. The race contrasts Robinson's sponsorship of the 2026 tax on income over $1 million with Bender's call for a low-tax state.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator and chair of Senate Ways & Means, in the Legislature since 2013, a public-health professional whose record centers the state budget, tax reform, housing and health care.
highlights: Chairs the Senate Ways & Means (budget) Committee; in the House 2013-2020 and the Senate since 2020 [S5]
Co-sponsored and voted for SB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and prime-sponsored the 2021 capital gains tax [S6][S7][S8]
Pledges to safeguard reproductive rights and defend immigrant and LGBTQ+ neighbors [S1]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025 parental-rights amendments) and EHB 1217 (rent increase limits) [S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, prime-sponsored the 2021 capital gains tax, and calls asking millionaires to pay a fair share her tax-reform achievement.

spending.basis: Cites record investments in housing, behavioral health, child care and health care and ties tax reform to sustaining public investment; as budget chair she also manages constraints, so not maximal.

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 cap on residential rent increases, cites record investments in affordable housing and is a former housing consortium director.

immigration.basis: Pamphlet pledges to defend immigrant neighbors; no specific enforcement or sanctuary measures named.

experience.basis: In the Legislature since 2013 and chair of Senate Ways & Means; opponent has never held office.

social.basis: Pledges to safeguard reproductive rights and defend LGBTQ+ neighbors, calls reproductive care a human right, will protect abortion access and objects to attacks on care for transgender people.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified the I-2081 parental-rights list, and says she helped pass the state's comprehensive sex-education law; no statement on notification or opt-outs.

candidates.summary: First-time Republican candidate, an electrician and small-business owner running on making Washington a low-tax, affordable state.
highlights: Wants Washington to be 'a reasonable, economical, and low-tax state' [S1]
Says Democrats in Olympia raise taxes to cover their own spending [S1]
No prior elected office; over thirty years in the electrical field [S1]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet statement centers lowering taxes and a 'low-tax state'; a single source.

spending.basis: Criticizes state spending as the driver of tax increases; no specific cuts or audits proposed.

experience.basis: States he has no previous elected experience and offers a 'blue-collar voice' against a long-serving incumbent.
